thesis: Janus Living rose about 2.3% to $30.75 on 10.1x volume. This run did not find a dated catalyst for today; its search confirmed no new pricing but did confirm repeated equity issuance this year: a $20 IPO in March and a 25M-share follow-on priced at $25 in June. The company's own filings flag conflicts with Healthpeak, which controls the REIT, shares its CEO, and supplies the manager under related-party agreements not negotiated at arm's length. Recurring issuance on top of an externally managed, controlled structure is an unresolved structural counter-case to the operating growth. With today's heavy volume unexplained, this is low; avoid.
invalidation: Issuance stops, Healthpeak's control and conflict structure is reduced, and operating growth carries through.

thesis: Bentley Systems reported Q3 2026 today (8-K). Revenue grew 12.2% to $421.5M (12.7% in constant currency), ARR reached $1.58B with 13% constant-currency growth, net revenue retention improved to 110%, the operating margin rose to 29.1% from 22.5%, and adjusted EPS of $0.36 beat the $0.33 consensus. The ARR growth outlook was raised to 12.5-13.5%. The stock rose about 3.0% to $44.94 on 3.8x volume, after a ~33% run over 60 days. Legal: the latest 10-Q reports no material pending litigation, the 2024 law-firm notice produced no filing this run found, and the convertible notes were repaid in January. This run found no restatement or equity raise. No specific fundamental counter-case was explicitly engaged and resolved beyond the run-up itself, which is price action, so this is medium.
invalidation: ARR growth decelerates below the raised range or net revenue retention slips, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$43.64).

thesis: Unity reported Q3 2026 today (8-K). Revenue rose to $622M from $471M, and the company posted its first GAAP profit since its IPO, $122M of net income. The adjusted EBITDA margin was 41%, free cash flow was $220M, and management guided to further year-over-year acceleration in Q4 revenue growth and margins. Grow Solutions (ads) rose to $457M from $318M. The stock rose about 15.0% to $48.85 on 5.1x volume. The counter-case is named but not resolved: growth is concentrated in the ad-network Grow segment, a competitive mobile-ad market, while Create grew only about 9%. Legal: the 2022 securities class action (N.D. Cal.) awaits a motion-to-dismiss ruling with no scheduled date found. This run found no restatement or new equity raise. This is medium.
invalidation: Grow revenue growth stalls or Q4 misses the acceleration guide, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$42.46).

thesis: Magnite reported Q3 2026 on Nov 4 after the close and rose about 20.6% today to $27.49 on 5.0x volume, near its 52-week high. Revenue rose 14% to $204.2M, and contribution ex-TAC rose 20% to $200.6M, above its $188-192M guide. CTV contribution grew 39% to $105.4M, and adjusted EPS of $0.33 beat the $0.28 consensus. Full-year contribution ex-TAC growth guidance was raised to about 17% from 13-14%. The counter-case is named but not resolved: the DV+ (display) segment grew only 5%, and the business remains exposed to the ad cycle. Magnite is the plaintiff in its antitrust damages suit against Google, so that is not a risk flag. This run found no restatement or equity raise. This is medium.
invalidation: CTV growth slows or Q4 contribution ex-TAC misses the $227-233M guide, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$22.79).

thesis: Rhythm reported Q3 2026 on Nov 3. IMCIVREE net revenue rose 29% sequentially to $92.1M, there were more than 700 patient start forms for acquired hypothalamic obesity, and the indication is approved in the US, EU and Japan. Even so, the stock fell 7.5% on the report as Needham cut its target, and it fell another 5.0% today to $105.17 on 5.0x volume. The financing tied to an LG Chem licensing amendment is not detailed in this run's sources. With strong launch metrics offset by a two-day ~12% decline this run could not explain, the evidence is unresolved, so this is low; avoid.
invalidation: The cause of the post-report selling is identified as benign and the hypothalamic-obesity launch keeps accelerating.

thesis: SS&C traded 5.1x volume and slipped about 1.6% to $78.28 after proposing a $1.0B private placement of convertible senior notes due 2031, reportedly to refinance 2027 debt. A pending convertible raise is a dilution-risk-level fact. Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.78 was essentially in line with the $1.77 consensus, so there is no offsetting fundamental catalyst. Legal: the Q2 2026 10-Q reports no material changes, and the DST 401(k) matters are legacy. With an in-line quarter plus a dilutive financing overhang, this is low; avoid.
invalidation: The notes price with limited dilution and organic growth accelerates.

thesis: CVR Energy reported a record Q3 2026 on Nov 3: net income of $570M ($5.67 per share), adjusted EPS of $4.00 and adjusted EBITDA of $582M, on historic refining margins. It also agreed to buy Marathon's St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries, targeting a year-end close. The stock fell about 7.4% today to $39.83 on 4.5x volume, and a MarketScreener feed lists a $750M share offering, which this run could not confirm in detail. A pending equity raise to fund a large acquisition is a dilution risk, and peak refining margins are cyclical. This is low; avoid.
invalidation: The acquisition closes on accretive terms with limited dilution and margins hold.

thesis: ADMA reported Q3 2026 on Nov 4 (8-K) and rose about 26.1% today to $13.22 on 4.5x volume. Revenue grew 5% to $141.1M, ASCENIV rose 31% to $124.7M, gross margin rose to 71%, and the company raised its adjusted earnings outlook while repurchasing shares. The counter-case is fundamental and unresolved, and it goes to revenue quality. BIVIGAM revenue fell on channel inventory pressure. A March 2026 Culper short report alleged channel stuffing and an undisclosed related-party distributor, and a securities class action was filed in D.N.J. (class period Aug 2024 - Mar 2026). No scheduled ruling was found and there is no confirmed finding, so no risk flag applies. With strong reported results set against an open channel-integrity allegation, the evidence is mixed, so this is low.
invalidation: The channel-stuffing allegations are substantiated or the class action advances, or BIVIGAM weakness spreads to ASCENIV.

thesis: Remitly reported a record Q3 2026 on Nov 4: revenue rose 22% to $509.8M, EPS of $0.30 beat the $0.28 estimate, and the full-year outlook was raised. Even so, the stock gapped down from $27.08 and closed about 20.4% lower at $21.55 on 4.1x volume. Coverage points to Q4 revenue guidance of about $532M, only in line with consensus, as the disappointment. Legal: 2024 law-firm investigation notices and a 2025 short-seller allegation have no filed action or scheduled step that this run found. With a beat offset by a sharp, unexplained derating, this is low; avoid.
invalidation: Q4 revenue lands well above the ~$532M guide and the selloff reverses on fundamentals.

thesis: Revolution Medicines fell about 11.0% to $177.74 on 4.1x volume on the day it reported Q3 2026, even as Piper Sandler raised its target to $222. Its RAS inhibitor daraxonrasib is marketed as RASONQUE, but an October FDA review raised efficacy questions in some KRAS mutations. The company raised equity and converts in April 2026 and set up a $1B ATM program in February. Coverage frames today's drop as a stock well above its moving averages being vulnerable to any setback. This run found no Q3 detail explaining the move, and the Delaware Nemeth suit, inherited as EQRx's successor, has no scheduled step. With the drop unexplained, this is low; avoid.
invalidation: Launch metrics or label clarity resolve the efficacy questions and the shares stabilize.

thesis: Liberty Media (Formula One Group, FWONK) reported Q3 2026 today and rose about 7.8% to $106.64 on 3.9x volume, near its 52-week high. Adjusted OIBDA rose 44% to $338M on seven races against six a year earlier, and the season count was revised up to 23. Bloomberg reports Liberty is acquiring John Malone's super-voting shares to simplify the structure. The counter-case is named but not resolved: revenue of about $1.12B missed estimates by roughly $120M, and net leverage is 3.0x. Legal: the EU's 2024-25 in-depth review of the MotoGP purchase and the older DOJ Andretti inquiry have no 2026 scheduled step that this run found. This run found no restatement or equity raise. This is medium.
invalidation: Revenue misses persist as race-count benefits fade, or the governance change dilutes holders, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$98.93).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 20). CLF fell another 12.3% to $11.27 after Wednesday's 9.2% drop, a two-day decline of about 21%. It closed below the ~$12.12 pre-report level, the thesis's stated price invalidation. This run found no company disclosure explaining the selloff; coverage shows only heavy put buying and bearish options positioning. The Oct 19 Q3 fundamentals behind the entry thesis (Q4 EBITDA guided to about $715M, 2027 above $4B) are not themselves contradicted. But the invalidation is met, and the counter-cases named in the prior thesis (steel-price and contract dependence, the Stelco/Canada dispute, high leverage) remain open, so the thesis no longer supports holding. The early-exit guard does not apply: the opening buy was more than 5 trading days ago. Exit.

Held position (opened Oct 22). ROIV fell about 4.2% to $36.63; this run found no new company disclosure for today. It remains above the ~$34.92 pre-announcement level. The thesis rests on the Oct 21 CLARITY Phase 3 results: brepocitinib met the primary and all key secondary endpoints in non-infectious uveitis, and the drug is already approved for dermatomyositis as Lisraya. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: the uveitis indication is not yet approved, and the sNDA is not planned until 1H 2027. Fiscal Q2 results on Nov 9 are the next scheduled event. This stays medium.
invalidation: Full CLARITY data or FDA feedback reveal a safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 28 on the Oct 27 proposal). Centene eased about 2.4% to $74.16 after Wednesday's analyst-driven rally to a 52-week high, and this run found no new company disclosure for today. It remains well above the ~$68.03 pre-report level. The thesis rests on the Oct 27 Q3 report (8-K): adjusted EPS of $0.58 against a ~$0.07-0.10 consensus and full-year guidance raised above $5.20. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: roughly $0.50 of non-recurring 2026 EPS, Medicaid membership declines and margin pressure, the 2027 Arkansas Medicaid expansion exit, and the Lunstrum v. Centene class action with no scheduled ruling. These cap this at medium.
invalidation: Medicaid cost trends worsen enough to put the raised guidance at risk, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$68.03).

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 3 on the Nov 2 proposal). NWL fell about 6.5% to $5.48, below the $5.82 entry, and this run's search found no new disclosure for today. It remains above the ~$5.08 pre-report invalidation level. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open and keep the evidence mixed. From the Oct 30 Q3 report: the operating cash flow outlook was cut about 62% to $150M, there are about $220M of inflation headwinds, a $101M impairment, and full-year adjusted EPS guidance was only maintained, set against 3.7% sales growth and a 90bp normalized margin gain. The early-exit guard applies (the opening buy was 2 trading days ago), and there is no new fact, so the direction stays long. This stays low, and the stop-loss and conviction-trim still protect the position.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the $0.17-0.19 EPS guide or the cash-flow outlook is cut again, a further impairment, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$5.08).
